item.text: I found a real cleanup in the current API: `sort(...)` now sorts by allocating a full copy and then copying it back, which is unnecessary work. I’m refactoring both public entry points to share one internal implementation and tightening the tests around that contract.

The public API now shares a single in-place implementation instead of copying work through `sortedCopy(...)`. I’m compiling and rerunning the demo plus the test harness to verify the refactor and the added edge cases.

Refactored the current API to remove an unnecessary full-array copy on the in-place path. In [BucketSort.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/039_bucket_sort/BucketSort.java:1), `sort(...)` and `sortedCopy(...)` now share a single private `sortInPlace(...)` implementation, so the mutating API no longer sorts by cloning and copying back.

I also extended [BucketSortTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/039_bucket_sort/BucketSortTest.java:1) with duplicate-value coverage and near-upper-bound coverage, which better exercises the bucket-index logic without changing the public behavior.

Verified with:
- `javac Main.java BucketSort.java BucketSortTest.java`
- `java Main`
- `java BucketSortTest`
